description: Guided A2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Map has the short /æ/ vowel. Mop has /ɑ/, men has /ɛ/, and mup is not a standard English word.
Neck has the short /ɛ/ vowel. Nick has /ɪ/, knack has /æ/, and nook has /ʊ/.
Dust has the /ʌ/ vowel. Desk has /ɛ/, dish has /ɪ/, and dusk has the same vowel but a different final consonant.
Shop begins with /ʃ/. Chop begins with /tʃ/, shot has the same first sound but a different ending, and stop begins with /st/.
Zip begins with voiced /z/. Sip begins with /s/, dip with /d/, and lip with /l/.
Vest begins with /v/, made with vocal-cord vibration. West begins with /w/, while best and test begin with /b/ and /t/.
Peace ends with /s/. Peak ends with /k/, peat with /t/, and peach with /tʃ/.
Bath ends with the unvoiced th sound /θ/. Back ends with /k/, bad with /d/, and bat with /t/.
Cage ends with /dʒ/. Cake ends with /k/, came with /m/, and case with /s/.
Train uses ai to spell the /eɪ/ vowel followed by /n/. Trail ends in /l/, trait in /t/, and tray has no final consonant.
Cheese uses ee to spell the long /i/ sound. Cheek and cheer share that vowel but have different endings; chess has /ɛ/.
Thumb begins with th pronounced /θ/ and ends with a silent b. Thump has a pronounced /p/, thug has a different ending, and hum begins with /h/.
